events.text: You bit your father's finger so hard he claimed you had a martial artist's jaw. Your mother said you were hungry.
variants: Your father let you chew on his finger once and regretted it loudly. He said you had a martial artist's jaw. Your mother said you were hungry.

events.text: A fever nearly took you in your second winter. The village healer sat up with you for three nights.
variants: In your second winter you burned with fever, and the village healer did not leave your side for three nights.

events.text: Your first word was 'sword'. Nobody in the family owns one. Nobody knows where you heard it.
You tried to arm-wrestle the neighbour's dog. The dog won. You were not discouraged.
You carve a sword from a branch and declare yourself the strongest under heaven. The chickens are not impressed.

effects.log: Your arms ache. Your heart sings.

ok.log: The rooster retreats. Word spreads among the village children.

fail.log: The rooster wins. Word spreads anyway.

events.text: A travelling storyteller tells the village about the Heavenly Demon, the Sword Saint, and the day a single swordsman held a mountain pass against a thousand men.

effects.log: That night you dream of mountain passes.

choices.text: Ask him if any of it is true

effects.log: He laughs. 'All of it. None of it. Go and find out.'

events.text: {npc} pushes you into the mud in front of the other children and laughs.

mem.note: threw me in the mud in front of everyone

ok.log: You throw {npc} in the mud instead. {He} will remember this.

fail.log: You lose, and eat more mud. Next time.

effects.log: You walk away. It burns more than any beating.

mem.note: shared your lunch with me when I was cruel

effects.log: {npc} stares at the rice ball as if it might bite. Then {he} eats it.

events.text: {npc} slips on the riverbank and goes under the fast water.

mem.note: pulled me out of the river when we were children

ok.log: You drag {npc} onto the bank, both of you coughing. {He} never forgets it.

mem.note: nearly drowned pulling me out of the river

fail.log: You both nearly drown. A fisherman pulls you out by your hair.
fail.deathCause: the fast water of the river

mem.note: ran for help when I was drowning

effects.log: You run faster than you have ever run. The adults get there in time.

events.text: Chasing a cat, you fall down an old dry well. At the bottom, under the leaves, is an oilcloth bundle: a thin book of breathing exercises.

effects.log: The characters are hard. You learn them anyway. Your breath begins to move differently.
Your father sells it for twenty taels and buys a pig. It is a very good pig.

events.text: A filthy old beggar at the edge of the village watches you train with a stick. 'Your stance is wrong,' {he} says. 'Your breathing is worse. Bring me a chicken and I will fix both.'

mem.note: brought me a stolen chicken when I was starving

effects.log: {npc} eats the chicken, bones and all. Then {he} teaches you to breathe. You have a master.

choices.text: Buy a chicken with your savings

mem.note: spent your last coins to feed an old beggar

effects.log: {npc} looks at the coins, then at you, a long time. 'Honest. Rare. Sit down.' You have a master.
{He} shrugs and wanders off. Years later you will hear what {he} was, and wonder.

events.text: The old monk who feeds the temple orphans notices you copying the monks' morning forms from behind a pillar.

effects.log: He teaches you the temple's breathing method. 'For health,' he says. You know better.

ok.log: You piece the method together from watching. The monk pretends not to notice.

fail.log: You learn the shapes but not the breath behind them.

events.text: An old beggar with a green bamboo staff watches you outrun two guards with a stolen bun. 'Fast legs,' he says. 'Wasted on buns.'

effects.log: He teaches you the Beggars' Union's footwork and breathing. The bun was worth it.

ok.log: You get away. Probably. He was smiling.

fail.log: He catches you with one finger on your collar, and teaches you anyway.

events.text: Your grandfather gives you a scorched manual wrapped in silk. 'All that is left of our sect. Someone destroyed us. One day you will learn who.'

effects.log: The manual smells of old smoke. You read it until the candle dies.

events.text: Your family's martial instructor tests the children. The elders watch, making notes on who is worth investing in.

ok.log: You impress the elders. They give you the family's inner breathing method early.

fail.log: You collapse in the last round. An elder writes something short in the ledger.

choices.text: Hold back and watch the others

effects.log: You learn more from watching than they do from fighting.

events.text: {npc} falls ill. The healer says only a mountain herb that grows on the cliffs above the village can help.

mem.note: climbed the cliffs for my medicine

ok.log: You come back bleeding with a fistful of the herb. {npc} lives.

fail.log: You fall. A woodcutter finds you. The herb is still in your fist, crushed.

choices.text: Sell your things to pay a herb gatherer

mem.note: sold everything you had for my medicine

effects.log: The gatherer climbs. Your mother lives. You own nothing, and do not mind.

choices.text: Stay by the bed and look after {npc}

mem.note: sat by my bed every night

effects.log: You fetch water, cool {npc}'s forehead and sleep on the floor beside the bed. It is a long, frightening winter, but the fever breaks at last. You are thinner by spring, and {npc} never forgets who stayed.

events.text: The Mount Hua Sect, one of the Orthodox Alliance's nine great sects, is holding its entrance test in the provincial town. Hundreds of children queue in the square. Elder {npc} watches from the steps.

ok.log: You pass. Elder {npc} taps your shoulder with a fan. 'This one is mine.' You are a disciple of the Mount Hua Sect.

fail.log: You fail the meridian test. On the road home you promise yourself: they will regret it.

effects.log: You watch the carts leave for town from the rooftop.

events.text: Monks of the Shaolin Temple arrive in the valley to choose novices. Their test is simple: carry two buckets of water up nine hundred steps without spilling.

ok.log: You reach the top with the buckets full and your legs shaking. Abbot's disciple {npc} nods once. You are a novice of the Shaolin Temple.

fail.log: You spill on step six hundred. The monks bow politely and leave.

effects.log: You keep your hair. It is very good hair.

events.text: When the children of the family come of age, they are formally entered into the clan's martial lineage. Elder {npc} will choose who trains under the inner hall.

ok.log: You win a place in the inner hall. Elder {npc} becomes your master. The cousins will not forgive you.

fail.log: Outer hall. Respectable. Nobody says the word 'disappointing' out loud.

events.text: Bandits of the Black Wind Stronghold ride into the village for their 'protection fee'. Their lieutenant, {npc}, sees you standing your ground instead of hiding. 'You. You have guts. Want to eat meat every day?'

effects.log: You ride out with the bandits. The village does not wave goodbye.

mem.note: turned down my offer in front of my men

effects.log: {npc} laughs. 'Your loss.' The fee is doubled this year.

mem.note: spat at my feet in front of my men

effects.log: {npc} beats you half to death, and remembers your face.

events.text: A woman in red visits the village at night, walks straight past a dozen houses and stops at yours. 'The blood in you is very old,' says {npc} of the Heavenly Demon Cult. 'It will wake whether you like it or not. Come, and learn to ride it.'

effects.log: You leave before dawn without a word. The Cult's mountain is colder than you imagined, and far more beautiful.
{npc} smiles. 'We will meet again. Blood always comes home.'

events.text: You have your own method now, and no sect. The murim is wide, and nobody is telling you where to stand.

effects.log: You buy a bamboo hat and a cheap sword. The road is your sect.
Not yet. Somewhere, a sect is waiting for someone exactly like you.

events.text: Word of you has reached the Wudang Sect. Elder {npc} arrives with an offer: an outer disciple's place, and a real sword manual. 'Late bloomers are rare. So are good swords.'

effects.log: You kneel to your new master. The manual is heavier than any sword.
{npc} bows. 'Wudang does not ask twice.'

events.text: Everyone your age with a sect is already gathering internal energy. You still have none. A retired guard in the tavern notices you staring at the swords on the wall.

effects.log: It is a guard's method, crude and slow. It is a method.

choices.text: Work his fields for a year in exchange

ok.log: A year of hoeing and breathing exercises. At the end of it, a thin thread of energy stirs below your navel.

fail.log: A year of hoeing. He teaches you the words, but the energy never comes. 'Some bodies are just bodies,' he says, kindly.

effects.log: You put the dream away like an old coat. Some nights you still dream of mountain passes.

events.text: A wandering physician from the south examines your wrist and frowns. 'Blocked meridians. I have seen worse. I can open them, but it will hurt like nothing you have ever felt, and it will cost 300 taels.'

effects.log: Forty days of needles and fire. When it ends, your energy flows like a river through a broken dam.

choices.text: Work for him as an assistant instead

ok.log: Two years carrying his herb chest. On the last night he keeps his promise.

fail.log: You learn a lot of medicine. He leaves without a word one morning.

effects.log: 'Stubborn,' he says. 'Good. You will need that.'
